title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: No past price increase of this magnitude showed uplift; recent weeks at $5.20 saw no lift vs baseline.

drivers.name: Supply delivery short
drivers.evidence: Supplier warning of short delivery; plausible demand reduction, but no prior data on impact. Shrink toward 1.0 due to uncertainty.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 30.3. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is raised 3.4% above regular (5.20 vs 5.03), which historically has not driven uplift—past price increases (e.g., 2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) showed no lift. The supplier warning of a short delivery implies supply risk, likely reducing demand (downside). The recent trend (27→32 units) reflects a seasonal ramp, already captured by the baseline. No past promotion effect is reliable (noise-adjusted x1.0). The classical model suggests no uplift, consistent with weak evidence. One past week with a price increase shows no lift. The downside risk from supply constraint is credible but uncertain. Shrink toward 1.0.

brief:
PRODUCT: Hot Cocoa Mix | category Grocery | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.20 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.03)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 30.3 | 5%-95%: 4.6 - 46.8 | 10%-90%: 9.0 - 46.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
